subject: Private offer: geo-tiered commit ladder and reseller fee smoothing
messages:
From: Claire Barnes <procurement@finedge.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 08:14:00 +0000
Subject: Private offer question — commit ladder across EU regions and reseller fee smoothing

Hi Rachel / Ben,

We're putting together an internal request for a private offer through AWS Marketplace for our EU operations. A few points we need aligned before procurement can move to PO: 

- Commit ladder: can Redwood provide a stepped commit structure (quarterly tiers) that allows us to escalate node-hour commitments over 12 months? We want a clear ladder for volume discounts if we cross thresholds mid-year.
- Geo-tiering: we operate in DE/FR/IE — does the private offer allow region-specific list price floors or do prices need to be harmonized across EU regions?
- Reseller fee smoothing: our reseller (CloudBridge) prefers a smoothing mechanism so they don't get variable payouts each month — they asked for a quarterly reconciliation model instead of immediate pass-through.
- Transit/marketplace fees: are there standard transit charges or pass-throughs in the invoice that we should expect (AWS marketplace list price vs invoice routed to reseller)?

Can you share a draft commit ladder and an explanation of how we could structure reseller fee smoothing (holdback / quarterly true-up / credits)? If helpful, we can do a 30m session with your team this week.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Barnes
Head of Procurement, FinEdge
procurement@finedge.io

(Attachment: initial-usage-profile.csv)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Claire Barnes <procurement@finedge.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 12:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private offer question — commit ladder across EU regions and reseller fee smoothing

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear outline. We've sketched a pragmatic approach and attached two stubs: commit-ladder-draft.xlsx (quarterly tiers + sample pricing) and reseller-fee-smoothing-proposal.pdf (ops playbook). High-level notes below.

1) Commit ladder (attached)
- 12-month horizon split into four quarterly thresholds (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4). Each quarter has a base commit and a mid-quarter uplift band that triggers a higher discount tier for remainder of quarter.
- Mid-quarter escalations are applied pro rata for the remainder of the quarter, with full-tier pricing from the next quarter onward.

2) Geo-tiering
- We can support region-specific list prices for DE/FR/IE in the private offer metadata. That said, major customers prefer harmonized EU pricing to simplify billing and compliance. We recommend region-specific list prices only if you have materially different usage or tax profiles per country.

3) Reseller fee smoothing (CloudBridge)
- Two operational options: a) invoice pass-through with monthly adjustments (high variability) or b) quarterly reconciliation with a 3–5% holdback applied monthly and true-up quarterly.
- Our proposal (attached) defaults to a 4% holdback with quarterly true-up credits invoiced by Redwood to the reseller. This preserves predictable cashflow for CloudBridge while keeping the bookkeeping simple for FinEdge.

4) Transit / marketplace fees
- AWS Marketplace will show the list price but routing and reseller payout depend on the private offer configuration. If you want reseller invoicing, we'll set invoice routing so CloudBridge receives the reseller portion and Redwood invoices FinEdge for the net amount (or vice versa depending on preferred flows). Expect standard marketplace transaction fees (we can provide a line-item estimate).

Next steps: can we lock a 30m call on Thu 24 Jun 10:00-10:30 BST? Ben/Jordan will join to cover deal ops. If you prefer, we can also include the AWS Marketplace rep to confirm routing.

Attaching: commit-ladder-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet) — contains example thresholds and net price columnseseller-fee-smoothing-proposal.pdf (ops summary)

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private offer question — commit ladder across EU regions and reseller fee smoothing

Rachel / Jordan / Claire — quick note from my side. For reseller smoothing I'd recommend aiming for a 3%–4% holdback with quarterly reconciliation. Operationally we do quarterly reconciliations (credit memos) to the reseller to avoid monthly variance.

For pricing anchoring, call out whether FinEdge wants asymmetric ramp (low early quarter commits then step-up) or even-step ladder — that will materially change early ARR recognition for you. If they want protection for CloudBridge, the holdback + quarterly true-up is the cleanest path.

Happy to discuss on the Thu call. I can bring our finance ops lead if needed.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Sales — EMEA, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Claire Barnes <procurement@finedge.io>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Private offer question — commit ladder across EU regions and reseller fee smoothing

Claire / team — forwarding the attachments and the short plan. Irene (legal) is looped in to confirm there are no procurement redlines on the holdback mechanics; Irene, quick ask: can legal sign off on a quarterly true-up clause that limits Redwood liability and allows a reseller credit memo flow? Also, confirm that region-specific list prices are permitted in the private offer (we believe so, but want legal confirmation for tax/invoice language).

Proposed timeline: if legal signs off by Fri 26 Jun, we can finalize the private offer draft for FinEdge and aim for PO week of 6 Jul. Claire: does that timeline work for you?

Jordan Blake
Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
